title: FancyZones "Move newly created windows..." makes new WSL2 GUI windows unresponsive
author: pearson
summary: With FancyZones' move-new-windows option enabled, WSLg application windows opened from a non-primary monitor become unresponsive after being moved.
next_action: Reproduce with current WSLg and trace the window move/position sequence.

confidence.rationale: The old report is highly reproducible, but current WSLg behavior must be checked.

judgment.rationale: The report supplies deterministic multi-monitor steps, a workaround, expected/actual behavior, and a diagnostic archive; the age of the report makes a current maintainer repro the appropriate next step.
evidence: The failure is conditional on the move-new-windows option.
The same WSLg application is responsive when opened on the primary display.
Changing the primary monitor stops FancyZones moving WSLg windows and avoids the unresponsive state.
A PowerToys diagnostic archive is attached.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with current WSLg and trace the window move/position sequence.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report strongly identifies the interaction boundary but not whether the defect is in FancyZones positioning, WSLg, or an obsolete Windows/WSLg build.

issue_context.summary: With FancyZones' move-new-windows option enabled, WSLg application windows opened from a non-primary monitor become unresponsive after being moved.
known_information: The original environment used Windows 11, WSL2/WSLg, Ubuntu 20.04, and three monitors.
The issue reproduced on any non-primary monitor, not only the rotated display.
inferences: Moving a newly created WSLg window across monitors during initialization may race its surface/input setup.
issue_context.analysis: Because the reporter already gave a complete reproduction and archive, the remaining work belongs on a current maintainer test system.
initial_investigation: Read the complete reproduction and workaround.
Confirmed current FancyZones still has new-window positioning logic and multi-monitor editor/runtime components.

actions.label: Reproduce WSLg new-window move
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact performs no upstream write.

reproduce.title: Move a new WSLg window to the active non-primary monitor
prerequisites: Current WSLg installation and a Linux GUI app
setup: Enable Move newly created windows to the current active monitor.
Keep one primary and one non-primary monitor available.
steps: Open a WSL terminal on the non-primary monitor.
Disable the move-new-windows option and repeat as the control case.
reproduce.expected_result: The WSLg window should remain responsive whether or not FancyZones moves it.
